title: [CQ-F04e] Daemon test fixtures approve with explicit revisions
description:
Objective: Prepare the daemon test suite for CQ-F04b (task-c619879ed9a643139c184fd5cb1ee888), which will make every human approval refuse an omitted expectedPlanRevision. Some tests approve a plan only as SETUP, not to pin legacy behavior: they call state.approveTask(taskId) with one argument, or send APPROVE_TASK with no expectedPlanRevision. Make each of them pass the task's stored revision explicitly (0 for a stamp-less row). That is valid both before and after F04b, so this lands with no behavior change.

Deliverable: these known setup sites, plus any others a grep finds outside the three excluded files below, now pass the explicit revision:
- packages/moe-daemon/src/state/StateManager.test.ts (2 sites)
- packages/moe-daemon/src/state/taskExecutionPolicy.test.ts (1)
- packages/moe-daemon/src/tools/taskTimestamps.test.ts (1)
- packages/moe-daemon/src/__e2e__/lifecycle.e2e.test.ts (1)
- packages/moe-daemon/src/server/executionPolicySnapshot.test.ts (1)

Not in scope:
- Production code.
- The legacy pins in server/planApproval.test.ts, server/planApproval.integration.test.ts and server/WebSocketServer.test.ts. CQ-F04b revises those under the human-approved CQ-F MODIFY_RAIL.
- Weakening or removing any assertion.

Verification command (fresh, exit 0 required): cd packages/moe-daemon && npm test
definitionOfDone: Every daemon test outside planApproval.test.ts, planApproval.integration.test.ts and WebSocketServer.test.ts that approves a plan passes an explicit expectedPlanRevision: the task's stored revision, or 0 for a stamp-less row. A grep finds no remaining token-free setup approval outside those three files.
No production file changes, and no assertion is weakened or removed: each edited test asserts what it asserted before.
Fresh verification `cd packages/moe-daemon && npm test` exits 0 and its output is supplied to complete_task.
taskRails: No direct .moe edits; no Git-write commands by agents; wrappers own landing.
Do not enable verified-local or claim isolation until all requisite implementation and certification gates pass.

implementationPlan.description:
PASS EXPLICIT REVISIONS AT EVERY SETUP APPROVAL. These are test-only edits; production code is untouched. Each token must equal the fixture's stored revision, or 0 when the fixture writes none. A wrong token turns the test into PLAN_REVISION_MISMATCH and the suite fails, so a green run proves the tokens are right. Read each fixture helper to get the value; never guess it.
- packages/moe-daemon/src/state/StateManager.test.ts: 'sets task status to WORKING' calls stateManager.approveTask('task-test123'), so pass the fixture's revision. Leave 'throws if task not found' as it is: the task lookup precedes every token check, so it is not an approval.
- packages/moe-daemon/src/tools/taskTimestamps.test.ts: 'manual approval sets planApprovedAt' calls h.state.approveTask('task-1'), so pass the fixture's revision.
- packages/moe-daemon/src/__e2e__/lifecycle.e2e.test.ts: the approveAndClaimWorker helper calls state.approveTask(taskId). Pass the task's current stored revision; reading it from state is fine in a test, because the scenario's reviewer saw exactly that.
- packages/moe-daemon/src/state/taskExecutionPolicy.test.ts: D4 (line ~774) and D6 (line ~796) call refusedNotReady(() => approve()). Pass the row's current revision, approve(1) if that is what the seeded row or submit() produced, so the test still proves the READINESS refusal once CQ-F04b puts an omission guard ahead of readiness. Leave the PROGRESSIONS row 'approveTask without a token' alone. It is a true legacy pin, and CQ-F04b converts it under the human-approved rail.
- packages/moe-daemon/src/server/executionPolicySnapshot.test.ts: in the W5 table, the row 'the UPDATE_TASK drag to WORKING' gets expectedPlanRevision: 1 in its payload (top-level payload key, not inside updates), so it still answers EXECUTION_PROFILE_NOT_READY. Leave the row 'APPROVE_TASK without a token' alone; CQ-F04b owns it.
Then grep packages/moe-daemon/src for approveTask( calls, APPROVE_TASK frames and UPDATE_TASK drags to WORKING in *.test.ts files outside planApproval.test.ts, planApproval.integration.test.ts and WebSocketServer.test.ts. Fix any other setup approval you find the same way.

VERIFY, ONCE. Run fresh in the local gate setup: Linux-native node_modules, lockfile unchanged, Linux-only PATH, MOE_* unset.
  cd packages/moe-daemon && npm test
It must exit 0; its output is the complete_task evidence. In the completion summary, paste the final grep. It shows that the only remaining token-free approvals outside the three pin files are exactly these three, with the reason for each:
(a) the not-found test, which is not an approval;
(b) the PROGRESSIONS row 'approveTask without a token', owned by CQ-F04b;
(c) the W5 row 'APPROVE_TASK without a token', owned by CQ-F04b.
With that, QA can check DoD 1 mechanically.

SELF-REVIEW (load adversarial-self-review) over the diff:
- Every edited test still asserts what it asserted before. No expectation, assertion or test is removed or loosened, and only the approval call's arguments changed.
- Every token equals the fixture's stored revision.
- No production file is in the diff.
- None of the project's globalRails forbidden patterns appears.
Error handling note: a refusal path such as refusedNotReady must still refuse for its original reason, now with a valid token. If any byte changed during review, re-run step 2's command and submit that fresh output.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered: Fold these edits into CQ-F04b? Rejected. It would push F04b past 10 files, and these edits are valid before AND after the behavior change, so they can land first and independently. The other choice was converting the two true legacy pins here. Also rejected: only F04b may change legacy behavior, under the human-approved rail. F04b's step 1 was amended to own them.
planningNotes.codebaseInsights: approveTask checks, in order: task lookup ('Task not found'), status, then the token (decode and compare against the stored revision, where an absent stamp reads as 0), then readiness, then a single write. So a not-found test is unaffected by any token rule, and a readiness-refusal test keeps its meaning only if its token is valid. In WebSocketServer.ts the UPDATE_TASK drag reads expectedPlanRevision from the top-level payload. The denylist strips it from updates.
planningNotes.risks:
- Guessing a token instead of reading the fixture's stored revision makes a test fail with PLAN_REVISION_MISMATCH. That failure is the safety net.
- Do not touch the three pin files or the two F04b-owned rows.
- CQ-F05 and CQ-I01 are in REVIEW but touch none of these five files.
